# Free LLM Models — Full Context for LLMs

> Free LLM Models is a searchable directory of currently free AI models across OpenRouter, Groq, Google AI Studio, Cerebras, Mistral, Hugging Face, and NVIDIA NIM. All data is machine-readable and refreshed from provider APIs.

The catalog is refreshed from provider APIs. Availability, limits, model policies, and pricing can change; verify important details with the provider before production use.

## Site

- Homepage: https://free-llm-models.custats.com/
- Canonical: https://free-llm-models.custats.com/
- Sitemap: https://free-llm-models.custats.com/sitemap.xml
- Robots: https://free-llm-models.custats.com/robots.txt
- GitHub: https://github.com/luongnv89/free-llm-models

## Machine-readable data

- Full catalog: https://free-llm-models.custats.com/free_models.json — aggregate with `models`, `archivedModels`, `providers`, `totalModels`, `fetchedAt`
- Per-provider index: https://free-llm-models.custats.com/models/index.json — provider files and counts
- Legacy snapshot: https://free-llm-models.custats.com/openrouter_free_models.json
- Per-provider files: https://free-llm-models.custats.com/models/{providerId}.json

Each model entry includes: `id`, `name`, `description`, `context_length`, `architecture.modality`, `pricing.prompt/completion`, `supported_parameters`, `providerId`, `addedToFreeList`, `popularity`.

## Pages

- FAQ: https://free-llm-models.custats.com/faq — API keys, first calls, rate limits, harness integrations, key security
- Archive: https://free-llm-models.custats.com/archive — former free models
- Model detail: https://free-llm-models.custats.com/model/{encoded-model-id} — per-model context, capabilities, and provider-specific setup recipes

## Providers

Supported providers (see README for env vars): openrouter (keyless), groq, google (Google AI Studio), cerebras, mistral, github-models, huggingface, nvidia-nim. Unconfigured providers are skipped with a warning.

## How to use the data

- Search/filter by provider, modality, context length, reasoning, tools in the UI.
- Fetch `free_models.json` for the full list, or `models/{providerId}.json` for per-provider.
- Model detail pages show OpenAI-compatible base URLs and harness recipes for Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode, Codex CLI.

## Harness setup

- Claude Code: set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (e.g. `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`) and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- Codex CLI: configure `~/.codex/config.toml` with `wire_api = "responses"` and `base_url`.
- Pi / OpenCode: use `/login` or env vars then select provider/model via their model pickers.

See the detail page's "Set up a coding harness" guide for provider-aware, copyable steps. Unsupported combinations explain the protocol gap and link to official docs.

## FAQ (verbatim)

Q: What are free models?
A: This site tracks AI language models available completely free of charge across multiple providers, with no cost for input or output tokens.

Q: How do I get an API key?
A: Each provider has its own signup. For OpenRouter, create an account, open API Keys in the dashboard, create a key, and store it securely.

Q: How do I make my first API call?
A: OpenRouter uses an OpenAI-compatible API format. Choose a free model, send a request with your API key, and read the model reply from the JSON response.

Q: What are the rate limits for free models?
A: Free models are rate limited. Limits vary by provider and model and can include requests per minute, daily limits, and lower queue priority.

Q: Are there any usage restrictions?
A: Check provider logging policies, terms of service, commercial-use permissions, and model availability before relying on a free model.

Q: Why do some models have an expiration date?
A: Some free models are promotional or trial versions. They may become paid, be replaced, or stop being available after the expiration date.

Q: How do I use OpenRouter with Claude Code?
A: OpenRouter integrates with Claude Code through an OpenRouter endpoint and API key configured in your shell profile or project settings.

Q: How do I use OpenRouter with LangChain?
A: LangChain can use OpenRouter through its OpenAI-compatible interface by setting the OpenRouter model, API key, and base URL.

Q: How do I use OpenRouter with the OpenAI SDK?
A: Since OpenRouter is OpenAI-compatible, configure the OpenAI SDK with the OpenRouter base URL and your API key.

Q: How do I use tool calling / function calling?
A: Define your tools, include them in the API request, and handle tool calls in the response. Check whether the model supports tools.

Q: How should I store my API key?
A: Store API keys in environment variables or a secret manager, never commit them to git, rotate them regularly, and limit their scope.

Q: What if my API key is compromised?
A: Revoke the compromised key immediately, create a new one, update applications, review account activity, and remove the secret from git history if necessary.

## Usage notes

- Free quotas are ephemeral and training-related: do not send sensitive code to free endpoints.
- For local usage, point harnesses at Ollama (`http://localhost:11434`) or LM Studio (`http://localhost:1234`) instead.

## Crawl & AI preferences

- `robots.txt` declares `Content-Signal: ai-train=no, search=yes, ai-input=no` and explicit `User-agent` rules for GPTBot, Claude-Web, etc.
- `User-agent: GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `CCBot`, `Bytespider`, `Google-Extended` are disallowed for training; search bots are allowed.

## Verification

- Sitemap and discovery URLs use `https://free-llm-models.custats.com/`.
- Structured data includes WebSite with SearchAction, Organization, Dataset, ItemList, WebPage, and per-model SoftwareApplication.
- Markdown negotiation (`Accept: text/markdown` → `text/markdown` + `x-markdown-tokens`) is served on Vercel; GitHub Pages documents it as Vercel-only.
